2608.04575.title: PhysMind: From Video to Executable Worlds for Training-Free Physical Reasoning
2608.04575.paper_summary: Reliable physical reasoning from video requires understanding how objects move, interact, and respond to interventions. Existing vision-language models (VLMs) often struggle to interpret these dynamics and reason reliably about future and counterfactual outcomes. We introduce PhysMind, a training-free agentic framework that constructs one reusable, question-agnostic executable world per video. PhysMind recovers a temporally consistent dynamic scene through object segmentation, mesh reconstruction, and 6D pose tracking, then fits analytic continuous-time dynamics and latent physical parameters without unrolling a time-stepped simulator. Given a question, it inspects, continues, or edits the world and answers from the resulting trajectories and interactions. Relative to direct chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning with the same VLM, PhysMind improves accuracy by 38.23 points on CLEVRER and 8.08 points on Physion++. On counterfactual questions, it exceeds the strongest evaluated VLM baseline, GPT-5.5, by 19.25 points.
2608.04575.paper_summary_zh: 可靠的視頻物理推理需要理解物體如何移動、互動以及對干預的反應。現有的視覺-語言模型（VLMs）通常難以解釋這些動態並可靠地推理未來和反事實的結果。我們介紹了PhysMind，一種無需訓練的代理框架，為每段視頻構建一個可重用的、與問題無關的可執行世界。PhysMind通過物體分割、網格重建和6D姿態追蹤恢復一個時間一致的動態場景，然後在不展開時間步模擬器的情況下擬合分析性連續時間動力學和潛在物理參數。給定一個問題，它檢查、繼續或編輯這個世界，並從結果的軌跡和互動中回答。相對於使用相同VLM的直接思維鏈（CoT）推理，PhysMind在CLEVRER上提高了38.23分的準確性，在Physion++上提高了8.08分。在反事實問題上，它超過了最強的評估VLM基準，GPT-5.5，達到了19.25分的提升。
